summary.text: Magnetite is a black or brownish-black iron oxide mineral and one of the main ores of iron.
Apart from extremely rare native iron, it is the most magnetic natural mineral on Earth, and magnetized lumps of it, called lodestone, first showed ancient peoples that magnetism exists.
Because it can preserve a record of Earth's magnetic field, magnetite has been a key tool in paleomagnetism, a science important to understanding plate tectonics.

items.prompt: Magnetite holds iron in two forms: ferrous iron, which carries less oxygen, and ferric iron, which carries more. What does this mix suggest about where it crystallized?

options.label: A place with no oxygen at all
A place packed with free oxygen
A place with middling oxygen levels
A place made only of seawater

items.explain: Having both ferrous and ferric iron points to crystallization where oxygen levels were intermediate, neither very low nor very high.

items.prompt: Long before anyone understood electricity, how did ancient peoples first find out that magnetism exists?

options.label: Lightning left metal tools able to cling
Natural rocks pulled small bits of iron
Rubbed amber picked up dry straw
Iron swords always pointed to the north

items.explain: Naturally magnetized magnetite, called lodestone, attracts small pieces of iron, and that is how ancient peoples first discovered magnetism.

items.prompt: A survey plane carrying a magnetometer flies over open country and records a strong local jump in magnetic intensity. What buried material could explain it?

options.label: A thick layer of rock salt
A large limestone cave
A buried seam of coal
A big body of magnetite

items.explain: Magnetite is strongly magnetic, so a large enough quantity of it shows up in aeromagnetic surveys made with a magnetometer.

items.prompt: Long ago, people found that a lodestone could serve as an early version of a familiar tool. Which one?

options.label: A sundial
A plumb line
A depth gauge
A compass

items.explain: Lodestones, naturally magnetized magnetite, were used as an early form of magnetic compass.

items.prompt: A student breaks open a piece of igneous rock and spots tiny grains of magnetite under a lens. How unusual is this find?

options.label: Not unusual; such grains are very common
Very rare; it forms only in meteorites
Impossible; it forms only in sediments
Rare; it forms only on beaches

items.explain: Small grains of magnetite are very common in igneous and metamorphic rocks.

items.prompt: Scientists studying how continents moved over time often turn to magnetite in old rocks. Why is it so helpful to them?

options.label: It keeps a record of Earth's magnetic field
It dissolves at a steady, known rate
It forms only right at plate edges
It glows when a plate starts moving

items.explain: Magnetite can preserve a record of Earth's magnetic field, which makes it a critical tool in paleomagnetism, a science important to plate tectonics.
